searchText: with the proposed api, is there a way to get validator set changes from epoch to epoch without getting all the validators and diff-ing? thought i'd ask here before opening another issue . 😛 prysm has this <https://api.prylabs.net/#/BeaconChain/GetValidatorActiveSetChanges> currently as an example <@!386151184869752834> there isn't at current. The reporting side of things (which is more user-focused) has been put on hold until we have nailed down the lower-level APIs. Once we have them it should alow us to work out what we need, what's available through the existing APIs, etc. ok. is it worth me opening an issue now about this endpoint <@144468805697929216> ? Probably worth doing so and explaining the use case so we have a note of it, yes these kind of API might be difficult to get right if they don't consider forks - ie the contents of an epoch diff will change depending on which history you're going down (say, if a validator is slashed) for example, specifying just `epoch` seems like an opening for race conditions <@449019668296892420> but that s just like eth1 apis and current endpoints work as well, if there s a fork, data between finalized and head might change. not sure how you could work around that... it seems to me that whoever is using the api will need to handle fork/reorgs as well if they want real time data, no? to a certain extent, yes - but what does it mean "to handle"? there are two ways: include the fork in the response or in the query basically, if you separate the "which fork are you on" query from "here's some information", we run into this problem as a node s local version of history could always be different than anothers for non finalized data i may be misinterpreting fork from what I can tell, the API above doesn't provide that information at all fork as in reorg fork ah, that s just an example for the return/data it gives, it should be modified to fit the spec well, if the example doesn't include this information, those building on top of it certainly won't consider it 😉 i m still not getting why it wouldn t work like any other endpoint, say https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs/#/Beacon/getStateValidators for instance sry this was just a tentative question, will make the issue better formulated... it's a very good question 🙂 I just noted that to make a diff, you need to know what you're diffing - the prysm api you linked just didn't seem to include that information - the eth2api has `state_id` for this purpose, so a diff would similarily have to have a way to pick out two points in history, is all thanks <@!449019668296892420> i ll think it over and try to describe better in an issue. much appreciated
